title: Unit cost & latency forensics playbook + wires
summary: Working playbook and wireframe notes for a token-level cost + latency forensic dashboard. Focus: fast triage flows for engineering/product to identify high-cost invocations, latency regressions, and candidate optimizations (batching, quantization, routing). This is an exploratory doc — sketches + prioritized backlog items for the next sprint.
goals: Enable triage of expensive invocations in <= 3 clicks
Surface cause hypotheses (model variant, prompt shape, client behavior) alongside raw metrics
Make per-token attribution actionable (link to rollout/pinning / autoscale settings)
Provide lightweight sampling to inspect token-level traces without full retention costs
user_personas_and_scenarios: Primary users: infra/serving engineer debugging latency spike, product manager validating cost regression from a rollout, platform engineer hunting hot routes for batching. Example scenario: After a canary deploy, 95th p50 latency rises 30% for route /chat. User opens dashboard, filters route, sees token heatmap spikes at generation step 2 -> discovers model variant fallback to larger model; rollback suggested.
wireframe_notes: Top-level layout: 3-column responsive grid. Left column: Filters + route list + small sparkline summary per route. Middle column (primary): Invocation timeline + stacked waterfall per token for a selected time window. Right column: Forensics pane with ranked hypotheses, sampled token traces, suggested actions (toggle autoscale/burst, pin older model). Key panels: 1) Route list with change indicator badges (cost delta, latency delta). 2) Timeline: aggregated invocations with overlaid cost and latency percentiles. 3) Token waterfall: horizontal bars per invocation showing prompt tokens (read-only), generation tokens, KV cache hits, with per-token microcost overlay. 4) Heatmap: token-position vs latency contribution (hotspots highlighted). 5) Sample inspector modal: shows raw prompt text (masked PII), token-by-token timing and kernel selection note. 6) Actionable card: recommended optimization (batch size 8, quantize to int8, route to cheaper variant) and estimated unit savings. Interaction notes: hover on token shows exact microcost and kernel; click opens sample trace. Keyboard shortcut 'f' focuses filter box.

user_flows: Flow A (engineer triage): open dashboard -> select route -> toggle 'show anomalous only' -> click top spike -> open sample inspector -> add note + create JIRA with link. Flow B (product review): open runbook view -> filter by tag 'canary' -> review top cost drivers -> accept suggested rollback action or schedule performance experiment.
metrics_and_kpis: Primary: cost per 1k tokens by route, 95th/50th/99th latency by route, % invocations with KV cache hits, median tokens generated per invocation. Secondary: time-to-detect (minutes), time-to-triage (minutes), estimated $ saved if suggested action applied.
privacy_and_sampling_policy: Default: sample 0.5% of invocations for full token trace; show aggregated microcosts for all invocations. PII masking rule: redact user messages longer than 50 chars by default; allow devs with permission to unmask for debugging. Retention: full traces retained 7 days by default, aggregates retained 90 days.
backlog_items: MVP: token waterfall + route filters + sample inspector modal
Add heatmap zoom + token-range selection for aggregations
Integrate suggested actions call-to-action with rollout API (pin/rollback) - auth gating
Store per-invocation kernel selection and expose as facet
Add anomaly detector job that tags spikes automatically and populates forensics pane
Experiment: live 'what-if' cost estimator when changing batch size or model variant
acceptance_criteria: MVP: can filter to a route, surface top 20 expensive invocations in a time window, open a sampled trace and see per-token timing and microcost. Suggested actions card should provide at least one actionable optimization with estimated cost delta. Dashboard loads < 2s for 1h time window with step=1m.
open_questions: Sampling: is 0.5% acceptable for SLO teams, or should sampling be route-weighted?
Data access: what RBAC level can view unmasked traces? tie to support vs eng roles?
Cost model alignment: should microcosts use actual infra unit prices or amortized allocation per tenant?
UI: do we show raw prompt tokens for enterprise customers by default or require explicit consent?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: exposing raw tokens causes privacy/regulatory issues. Mitigation: strict default masking + audit logs + opt-in unmask with justification. Risk: perf overhead of computing token-level attribution on the fly. Mitigation: precompute lightweight attributions and sample heavy traces asynchronously.
